subject: URGENT: StreamPay production latency and 5xx spike — suspected NAT/peering bottleneck
messages:
From: Heather O'Neill <heather.oneill@streampay.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carl Mendes <carl.mendes@streampay.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High latency & 500s across inference calls — urgent

Ava,

We started seeing a sustained latency increase and a rise in 5xx errors from Redwood-backed inference endpoints around 08:45 PDT. Throttling our traffic briefly reduces errors, but when we go back to normal volume the errors/latency spike again. This is impacting checkout validation (real-time fraud checks).

Quick data:
- 08:40–09:00 PDT: p95 latency jumped from ~180ms to ~1.6s
- 08:45–09:10 PDT: ~12% 5xx rate on /v1/generate for model rwd-3b
- We captured request ids and an example trace — attaching the tail logs.

Can you triage and loop in whoever needs to be involved? We need an ETA or a mitigation path (traffic routing, failover to smaller model, anything). This is affecting live payments.

Heather
Heather O'Neill
Head of Platform Reliability, StreamPay
Attachments: streampay_500s_log_tail.txt (text)
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: Heather O'Neill <heather.oneill@streampay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High latency & 500s across inference calls — urgent

Heather — thanks for the quick flag. I copied Ben from our networking infra team and opened an internal investigation ticket (PD-9134).
Immediate actions:
- Can you confirm whether the client IPs are from your peered VPC or from public internet? That helps narrow NAT/peering vs. upstream proxy issues.
- We will look at VPC peering counters and NAT translation queue metrics now.

I will follow up with a short update within 30 minutes. Apologies for the impact — prioritizing.

Ava Chen
Customer Success, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | ava_chen@redwood.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: (internal)
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: High latency & 500s across inference calls — urgent

Quick findings from initial triage:
- Observed NAT translation queue growth and connection reset spikes on the egress cluster servicing StreamPay's peered subnet (us-west-2 peering endpoint).
- DNS lookups for an internal proxy cluster show increased lookup latency and intermittent NXDOMAINs around the same timeframe.
- Proxy side (our edge-proxy pool) returned bursts of 502/504 correlated with the NAT queue saturation.
- Packet capture (attached) shows repeated SYN retransmits and TCP resets between our egress NAT and StreamPay's peering IP block.

Proposed mitigation (short-term):
1) Temporarily route StreamPay's traffic to an alternate egress pool (us-west-2-b) with lower NAT pressure. I can schedule a reroute now, needs coordination with infra runbook.
2) If reroute not possible quickly, enable aggressive keepalive and connection reuse hints by returning a short-lived 302 to clients to re-open connections to a different edge. (requires client cooperation).

I'll start the reroute exercise now and report back. Attaching packet capture and peering-config snapshot.

Attachments: packet_capture_20270315.pcap, peering-configs-20270315.pdf

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: High latency & 500s across inference calls — urgent

Ben/Ava — thanks for the triage. Ben: please proceed with the reroute ASAP and confirm expected timeframe for DNS TTL fallout. Carl (StreamPay) is unlikely to accept a client-side change quickly.
Operational ask: this is hitting a high-value customer and StreamPay is already pulling engineers into incident calls. I'm escalating to Marissa for exec awareness and to coordinate any credit/compensation conversation.

Summary for execs (for visibility):
- Impact: sustained p95 latency ~1.6s, 5xx spike ~12% from 08:45–ongoing; affects fraud validation path and checkout success.
- Root cause hypothesis: transient NAT exhaustion + DNS lookup amplification hitting our egress/proxy cluster servicing their peered VPC.
- Immediate mitigation: reroute to lower-loaded egress pool (pending), increase NAT pool capacity mid-term, audit peering config.
- Customer ask: ETA and mitigation; possible SLA credit.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Heather O'Neill <heather.oneill@streampay.com>, Carl Mendes <carl.mendes@streampay.com>
Cc: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 08:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Executive update: StreamPay production impact & next steps

Heather/Carl — I'm Marissa, head of Sales Operations. I'm joining this thread to ensure executive alignment and speed up any cross-functional approvals. First, thank you for surfacing this and for the packet/logs — they were helpful.
What we have done so far:
- Ben initiated a controlled reroute to egress pool us-west-2-b at 07:55 PDT; initial telemetry shows drop in 5xx and p95 trending back toward baseline.
- We are preparing a targeted peering config audit and increasing NAT allocation for your peered subnet.
- Open incident PD-9134 and internal doc: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBcD-peering-audit

Next steps and asks from StreamPay:
- Our team will finalize the peering config changes and confirm a non-disruptive window.
- We expect to propose a one-time service credit given the severity. I will coordinate with finance and your procurement contact on that.

ETA: Ben expects the reroute to fully mitigate within 30–45 minutes after cutover; permanent peering tweak timeline 48–72 hours. I will ensure a 1:1 postmortem and long-term prevention plan.

If you want a short exec-to-exec call, I'm available today between 12:00–16:00 PDT.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | marissa_cole@redwood.ai
From: Carl Mendes <carl.mendes@streampay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Heather O'Neill <heather.oneill@streampay.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Executive update: StreamPay production impact & next steps

Marissa/Ava/Team — thanks for the rapid response and clarity. We confirmed that the reroute to us-west-2-b reduced p95 to ~210ms and 5xx fell below 0.5% within 20 minutes of the change. Our SREs observed fewer SYN retransmits after the cutover.
We appreciate the proposed credit and would like the postmortem and peering audit as soon as possible. We'll schedule a follow-up call for Thursday morning to review the fix and the long-term plan.

Heather asked me to attach the final sample request IDs — she also confirmed that their checkout failures rate dropped to near-zero post-mitigation.

Thanks again — will await your postmortem.

Carl Mendes
Senior SRE, StreamPay
Attachments: streampay_final_request_ids.txt (text)
